_note: Every model assumption, with the value used, a plausible range and its source. status: sourced = value taken from the cited work; derived = calculated from the cited work; assumption = our choice, shown as such on the page.

uv_index_irradiance.unit: W/m2 erythemally weighted per UV index unit
uv_index_irradiance.source: WHO (2002). Global Solar UV Index: A Practical Guide. WHO/SDE/OEH/02.2

med_by_skin_type.source: Fajuyigbe D, Young AR (2016). The impact of skin colour on human photobiological responses. Pigment Cell Melanoma Res 29(6):607-18. doi:10.1111/pcmr.12511 (Table 1)
med_by_skin_type.note: Types V and VI are poorly studied. Self-reported skin type predicts measured MED poorly (Falk 2011, doi:10.1111/j.1600-0781.2011.00599.x), which is why each simulated person varies around these values.

med_person_variation.note: Spread of individual sensitivity within a skin type. Wide on purpose, given Falk 2011.

test_dose.source: ISO 24444:2019 Cosmetics - Sun protection test methods - In vivo determination of the SPF

reapply_interval.source: Cancer Council Australia, Sunscreen advice (reapply every 2 hours and after swimming, sweating or towel-drying)

amount_applied_default.source: Autier P et al. (2001). Quantity of sunscreen used by European students. Br J Dermatol 144(2):288-91. doi:10.1046/j.1365-2133.2001.04016.x (median 0.39); review: Petersen B, Wulf HC (2014). Application of sunscreen - theory and reality. Photodermatol Photoimmunol Photomed 30:96-101. doi:10.1111/phpp.12099

sources: Schalka S et al. (2009). Photodermatol Photoimmunol Photomed 25(4):175-80. doi:10.1111/j.1600-0781.2009.00408.x
Bimczok R et al. (2007). Skin Pharmacol Physiol 20(1):57-64. doi:10.1159/000096173
Ou-Yang H et al. (2012). J Am Acad Dermatol 67(6):1220-7. doi:10.1016/j.jaad.2012.02.029 (industry-funded)

spf_vs_amount.note: No review settles which model is right; studies of high-SPF products lean linear. The simulation gives each person one model at random, and the page shows both.

relax.basis: Ruvolo 2020: no measurable loss over 6 h at rest

sport.basis: Ruvolo 2020: SPF 50 fell to about 30 after 6 h of sweating

beach.basis: Bodekaer 2008: SPF down 55-58% after 8 h of activity and bathing

sources: Bodekaer M et al. (2008). Sun protection factor persistence during a day with physical activity and bathing. Photodermatol Photoimmunol Photomed 24(6):296-300. doi:10.1111/j.1600-0781.2008.00379.x
Ruvolo E, Aeschliman L, Cole C (2020). Evaluation of sunscreen efficacy over time and re-application. Photodermatol Photoimmunol Photomed 36(3):192-9. doi:10.1111/phpp.12535 (industry-funded)
spf_half_life_hours.note: Weak evidence: two small studies. Shown as a range on the page.

product_spf_variation.unit: lognormal sigma around the label SPF
product_spf_variation.context: CHOICE (June 2025) tested 20 products labelled SPF 50 or 50+; 16 measured below their label, with results from SPF 4 to 72. choice.com.au/about-us/media/media-releases/2025/june/16-of-20-sunscreens-didnt
product_spf_variation.note: No published inter-laboratory spread found; this value is illustrative.

uv_clock.note: ARPANSA timestamps do not shift for daylight saving (Sydney's January peak centres on 12:06, matching solar noon in AEST). The page adds one hour in daylight-saving months for NSW, ACT, VIC, TAS and SA.
